title: Veins - The First Artery
author: snooze00R
selftext:
Veins is a vertical slice of a first-person RPG and immersive sim, made by one solo developer working with AI assistance: Henry IX.

One Artery. Three depths. Nine floors.

It's also one HTML file. No engine, no build, no framework, no dependencies, no asset folder. The pixel art, the sprites, the fonts, the sound and the music are all generated at runtime in JavaScript and Web Audio. Nothing is loaded from disk.

I made it in a week because I wanted to find out whether a room that remembers could still work when the room is generating itself.

That's essentially the whole experiment. I wanted to make a game where it felt like how you play actually mattered, and this is the magic system I've always dreamed of building. Not a spell list you pick from, a set of rules the world runs on and you get to poke at.

You can sleep someone, calm them, cleanse them, subdue them, bind them, or pick their pockets while they're unconscious. You can kill them, obviously. The Rat King has seven possible endings from one encounter.

There are multiple solutions to problems, multiple endings, and a lot of tools that can interact with each other in ways I hope feel less like choosing a dialogue option and more like figuring out what the room will let you get away with.

AI-assisted throughout: the code (a single HTML file with no build) and the runtime asset generation for pixel art, sprites, fonts, sound and music were developed together with AI. Nothing is loaded from disk.

Everything you see and hear is generated at runtime in JavaScript and Web Audio.

Content warnings: Body horror / gore / violence / possession / rot / blood magic / animal death (rats)

Features

Magic

Nine schools. Six aspects. Dual casting. Spellbound items. Grimoire slots. Will and resistance. Forbidden arts.

Mercy

Sleep. Calm. Cleanse. Subdue. Rest. Bind. Pickpocket the unaware.

Combat

Light and heavy attacks. Parrying. Blocking. Dodging by load. Stamina. Reach, arc, pierce.

Ground

Fire, water, blood, fat, spores, rot, ice, ash, rubble, mist.

They react with each other, with the room, and with what you do in it.

World

Cracked stone. Rolling barrels. Braziers that can be lit and doused. Bone piles that rise unless burned or rested. Pods. Cracks. Secret stones. Rune circles. Warded gates.

Skills

Learn by doing. Weapon mains and families. Schools and aspects. Tongues. Crafting. Dual casting. Death.

Items

Quality. Rarity. Makes. Affixes. Enchantments. Affinities. Unique effects. Anomalies.

Crafting

Salvage. Patterns. Catalysts. Benches. Hone levels.

Death & Time

Revival. Grudge. Infection spread. Unrest. Rot. Slow. Rewind. Stasis. Feign death.

Divination

Read. Find. See through stone. See ahead. Sever fate. Bind fate. Ordain. A deck.

People

Trade. Quests. Bounties. Banter. Favour. Beast tongue.

Run

Difficulty tiers. Champions. Feats. Endings. A gallery. A journal. A map.

I made it alone, made it with AI, and made it as a love letter to the games that made me want to build one.

Any feedback at all is welcome. Game balance notes are the thing I can act on fastest, but I'm also curious what this sub thinks of the pipeline. The runtime-everything approach is the part I'd want to hear about if I were on your side of the screen. Whether it scales past a slice, whether there's a point where generating at runtime stops making sense, what you'd have done differently. If anyone here has shipped something on a similar setup I'd like to know what surprised you.

Happy to adjust anything above if it doesn't fit the sub.

Thanks for getting to the end. This has been a real passion project, and I hope you enjoy it.

Free on Steam if it gets there, donation-supported, always free to play.
